With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of activity and employment have continued to strengthen—consistent with New Keynesian policy guidance (e.g., Clarida, Galí, Gertler) that keeping rates low at the effective lower bound and using balance-sheet tools supports the recovery. The Committee’s average-inflation-targeting framework—allowing inflation to run moderately above 2% so the average returns to target—aims to anchor expectations near 2%, a commitment-style approach emphasized in the modern monetary literature and reinforced by the credit channel of QE (Bernanke-Gertler). That said, describing current inflation as “transitory” warrants caution: sticky-information models (Mankiw-Reis) imply gradual price adjustment, and real-time mismeasurement risks (Orphanides) can lead to policy reacting too late if inflation proves persistent; the Taylor principle underscores that policy must eventually respond more than one-for-one to sustained inflation. The signal that tapering “may soon be warranted” seeks to preserve accommodative financial conditions while reducing the risk of an expectations drift, in line with rule-like guidance and evidence on long-rate sensitivity to forward guidance and purchases (Cochrane-Piazzesi). Overall tone: constructive but risk-aware.
